newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia eyes expansion of debt market.
newsitem.headline: Colombia eyes expansion of debt market.

text.p: The Colombian government is considering a major expansion of its fledgling debt market to lower its dependency on foreign loans as the primary source of public finances, a top finance ministry official said.

Clemente del Valle, the ministry's director of Public Credit, said the revamped debt market could make its debut by early next year and it would be based along lines of the U.S. Treasury market and bond markets in several European capitals.
Colombia's public debt market, born out of a constitutional ban on central bank lending to the government in 1991, is still in its infancy.
Del Valle, who spoke in a Reuter interview, said the government plan was to expand it considerably and open it up to the laws of supply and demand.
Sixty-five percent of government financing is currently raised through foreign debt issues while the other 35 percent stems from the sale of Treasury bonds known as TES.
"The idea is to reverse that trend, as is the case in developed countries, where most necessary financing is obtained through the domestic market," Del Valle said.
He added that the government would seek to put a premium on "transparency" in the revamped Treasury market.

Only $4.5 billion in debt has been issued on Colombia's fixed-income market so far, and 70 percent of all operations are handled in pre-arranged deals between stock brokers and leading Colombian companies, including banks and financial institutions, many of which belong to the public sector.
"We're already talking with banks and financial corporations, as well as presidents of the stock exchanges, to forge ahead with the establishment of a debt market," Del Valle said.
He did not say whether the government would move to lift many of the existing restrictions on foreign investment in the fixed- income market. -- Javier Mozzo, Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944
